correctness.rationale: Every Hermitian two-by-two matrix of fixed trace \(t\) is \(tI/2+v\cdot\sigma\). Spectral calculus yields an exact inside/outside radial formula; the outside derivative in radial/tangential directions has norm \(\sqrt{1+(t/(2r))^2}\), and the inside derivative has norm one. Integration gives the global upper bound, a boundary-limit directional witness proves sharpness at each nonzero trace, and strict derivative bounds away from finitely many boundary crossings yield nonattainment. At zero trace the modulus is scalar and the reverse triangle inequality gives sharp one. The included checker tests 16,000 pairs and numerical boundary witnesses but does not replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The precise same-trace two-level modulus is a natural first noncommutative test case for operator absolute-value sensitivity, especially trace-conserving perturbations. The sharp discontinuity between trace-zero and every nonzero slice, exact spectral-gap-dependent local gain, and nonattainment at the rank-one boundary pinpoint a structural instability that neither a generic norm-comparison estimate nor unrestricted failure of operator Lipschitzness resolves. The quantifier is all complex Hermitian two-by-two matrices with equal trace.
